study type: Secondary analysis of a multicenter cohort
cohort: 21,114 individuals delivering at 17 US hospitals, excluding those with antepartum VTE, antepartum anticoagulation, or known SARS-CoV-2 infection
finding: While cesarean delivery, hysterectomy, and obesity were associated with increased postpartum thromboprophylaxis administration, it was not significantly linked to adverse outcomes like surgical site infection, bleeding, or readmission.
mod_finding: The frequency of postpartum pharmacologic thromboprophylaxis was 29.8% following cesarean and 3.5% following vaginal delivery.
mod_following: The frequency of postpartum pharmacologic thromboprophylaxis receipt was 29.8% following cesarean and 3.5% following vaginal delivery.
